name: ETF Common Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary and are subject to change.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline for most scholarships was March 15, 2026 (applications opened December 15, 2025). A few funds use separate windows.
apply: Create an ETF scholarship portal account, complete common application and all matched-fund supplemental questions. Upload required attachments; request any fund-required recommendation early, since application is incomplete until received. Separate applications/windows apply to named disability, student-support, law and visual-arts funds.
eligibility: East Tennessee students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Need-based funds accept FAFSA Submission Summary or Federal Student Aid Estimator results; inability to file due to citizenship/immigration does not disqualify applicants from many funds. No late/incomplete applications; award payments go directly to school. FAQ still carries a 2025 deadline, while application page lists 2026; neither establishes 2027.

name: NDCF scholarships
value: Donor scholarships with varying individual amounts; directory marks some below $500 or $300. John D. Weis example lists $1,000-$20,000 depending on applicants and funds, with annual reapplication.
deadline: Deadlines differ by fund. John D. Weis lists January 1-April 1 without year; this does not establish all funds’ 2027 windows.
apply: Apply to each scholarship separately per its page; many use the NDCF scholarship portal (Grant Interface) and some use mailed forms.
eligibility: Scholarships are organized by college, statewide, county and community criteria, mainly North Dakota with some cross-border school/county funds. Each sets its own residency, level, major, merit, need and required materials.
notes: Directory reports over $1 million aggregate awards, not an individual award. Check each fund’s instructions and firm deadline. Do not copy identical answers across different funds. Weis example supports students who lost a legal parent/guardian, including ND school/home/GED graduates or current accredited college/trade students.

provider: The Community Foundation for McHenry County
name: CFMC scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships with varying amounts and renewal rules. Current examples include $2,000 one-time, $2,500 one-time and $8,000 total ($2,000 annually for four years); other funds list variable awards.
deadline: Most scholarship opportunities open November 30, 2026, and close January 31, 2027. Some funds use other windows.
apply: Log in to the CFMC Scholarship Portal, take the eligibility quiz for each scholarship, and complete the full application if eligible.
eligibility: Students tied to named Illinois schools/communities, mainly McHenry County; some funds serve Rolling Meadows/Wauconda and current library employees pursuing graduate study. Each fund has separate GPA, need, service, study and renewal criteria; no universal county-residency or GPA minimum.
notes: Most portal awards open November 30, 2026 and close January 31, 2027; some external funds still list 2026 dates and distinct processes. Notifications late March/early April 2027. Check the chosen fund’s page; this listing is a scholarship collection.

name: CFNEIA scholarships
value: Donor scholarships with varying amounts; most cover one year, while some are two-year, four-year or renewable. Confirm the chosen fund’s amount and renewal criteria.
deadline: Application window opens January 10; page says complete 2027 process details will be posted then. Closing date not published. FAQ differs on required references: recommends by application deadline but permits receipt within one week after it; confirm the fund’s deadline.
apply: Create scholarship account and complete common application plus matched-fund supplements. Upload current unofficial transcript and financial information when needed. Some funds require a nonfamily reference, submitted directly by recommender through emailed link; external funds apply through school/community groups.
eligibility: High-school seniors, college students and adult learners planning college/university/trade/community-college study in fall. Fund-specific region, school, major, merit, need and demographic criteria apply; some are achievement-based without need.
notes: FAFSA summary optional for collection, but needed for many need-based funds; confirmation email with SAI accepted if summary pending. Award acceptance requires acceptance/college forms, proof of enrollment and donor thank-you; admission alone not proof. Results generally May/mid-June. Removed old aggregate-average award estimate.

name: QCCF scholarships
value: Individual scholarships range from $500 to $11,000 annually in the current FAQ; roughly half one-time and half renewable while criteria continue. Partial educational support; funds may cover tuition, fees, books and room/board subject to each fund.
deadline: Opens November 1, 2026. Auto Show applications and all supplements due January 17, 2027 at 11:59 p.m.; other applications/supplements due February 15, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. No time zone stated. Award recipients’ information sheet due June 15, 2027; payments July-August 2027.
apply: Create free online account and complete universal application to match funds, then submit every selected fund with transcripts, fund-specific essay and recommendation uploads. Auto Show requires two recommendations; others require one with optional second. Need-based funds require FAFSA summary/SAI. All documents included online by deadline; no late applications.
eligibility: Unless a fund states otherwise, live in, attended high school in, or attend college/graduate school in Rock Island County, Illinois or Scott County, Iowa. Other donor and affiliate criteria vary. Any citizenship/documentation status unless specific fund restricts it; undergraduate/graduate and trade opportunities vary.
notes: Collection of distinct awards, not one uniform scholarship. Funds paid to U.S.-incorporated educational institutions; direct foreign-institution enrollment unfunded, though eligible U.S.-institution study abroad possible. Renew only while the chosen fund’s criteria continue. Foundation’s $856,327 award total is aggregate funding.

name: LCF scholarships
value: Individual donor awards vary; current portal examples include $400-$5,000, one-time or renewable with each fund’s conditions/reapplication. Listed values may change before next cycle opens.
deadline: Next scholarship cycle opens December 15, 2026. Portal-wide 2027 closing date not published; check each opportunity. Current-cycle acceptance/disbursement form due July 31 without explicit year.
apply: Complete the General Application in the LCF AcademicWorks portal, then apply to recommended opportunities.
eligibility: Mainly Lancaster County, Nebraska students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: 93 funds benefit Lancaster County and students across Nebraska; no common GPA minimum. Foundation reports 299 recipients and over $606,000 aggregate in 2025. Portal values may change; new and renewal recipients complete required acceptance form before payment directly to school.

name: Wichita Foundation scholarships
value: Individual donor award amounts vary; current examples include $400, $500, $1,000, $1,200, $1,500, $2,000 and $2,500. Some permit one additional year through reapplication; others have separate renewal rules.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 cycle opened January 1, 2026, with applications due March 31, 2026, unless otherwise noted.
apply: Complete the general application in the Wichita Foundation Scholarship Portal (Grant Interface), then answer added questions for each matched scholarship.
eligibility: Kansas statewide and named local-school/zip-code funds, with fund-specific GPA, field, need and activities. Some require unweighted GPA 2.5/3.0; Evergy example uses weighted GPA 2.0. No collection-wide GPA minimum.
notes: Some funds require personal essays and financial-need review; others have different criteria. Submit each matched scholarship separately. Confirm the selected fund’s financial documents rather than treating FAFSA as universal.

provider: Boreal Waters Community Foundation (formerly Duluth Superior Area Community Foundation)
name: Boreal Waters scholarship portal
value: Individual donor scholarship amounts and renewal criteria vary; collection supports college, trade and returning-adult education. Confirm each matched award.
deadline: The universal application opens December 1, 2026 and closes February 9, 2027 at 11:59 p.m.; award notification by April 30, 2027. The application-page instruction saying February 29, 2027 is an impossible date and conflicts with the same page’s headline and timeline plus the separate official scholarship directory. Check the portal for fund-specific exceptions.
apply: Create student portal profile, complete eligibility quiz/universal application, then select matched awards and complete any added questions. Gather college/program/field/background details and financial information where requested.
eligibility: Students living in northeast Minnesota or northwest Wisconsin who plan to attend a college, university, community or technical college, or trade school. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: No ACT/SAT scores required. Foundation reports over $800,000 annual aggregate funding, not an individual award. Timeline plans payments by July 30 and December 30, 2027, but contradictory deadline instructions require confirmation.

provider: Community Foundation for the Fox Valley Region
name: CFFVR scholarship portal
value: Over 300 donor scholarships with fund-specific individual amounts, duration and renewal. Read each Scholarship Profile for payment procedures and continued eligibility.
deadline: Most portal applications open December 14, with year unstated. Published 2027 schedule: main universal application March 1, 2027; named fund deadlines February 1 through December 1, 2027, plus rolling awards. Check the chosen fund’s listed date; no common deadline/time zone.
apply: Use a long-term personal email for free portal account. Complete appropriate universal application once, then any matched supplemental applications; other funds apply through school guidance office. Read each Scholarship Profile for required materials. No limit on eligible applications.
eligibility: Funds serve high-school seniors, homeschool students, current college/nontraditional students and employee dependents. Geography, GPA, majors, need, citizenship and enrollment vary; generally at least six college credits, with institution-system adjustments possible. No common statewide residence/GPA cutoff.
notes: Foundation advertises over $2 million aggregate funding. One-time and renewable awards differ; recipients must verify continued eligibility between renewable payments. FAFSA where individual fund requires need information.

name: CICF scholarships
value: Individual award amounts depend on fund size and qualified applicants. Educational expenses may include tuition/required fees and, for some funds, books or room/board. Duration and renewal vary by fund.
deadline: General applications November 2, 2026-February 1, 2027; Church, Church, Hittle + Antrim October 14, 2026-January 2, 2027; Crooked Stick table April 15, 2026-June 3, 2027. Some individual descriptions still contain conflicting 2026/2027 labels; confirm fund-specific dates. No time zone stated.
apply: Gather current transcript, financial information (FAFSA, college aid letters/income) and contact details for two references. Create SmartSimple scholarship account, complete profile and submit selected eligible scholarships with all required materials by fund deadline. Follow award payment/enrollment/reporting instructions.
eligibility: Mainly central Indiana students with donor-specific residency, institution, major, GPA, need and affiliation rules. Some employee-dependent funds accept applicants in any state. Undocumented students may apply if individual criteria met; criminal history is not asked. No universal GPA or financial-need cutoff.
notes: 2024 total of $2.1 million across 211 scholarships is aggregate. Current page combines new 2027 schedule with older eligibility/date text in some fund sections. Lilly Endowment has separate nomination application and is listed separately.

name: Cleveland Foundation Scholarships (via College Now Greater Cleveland)
value: More than 60 donor scholarship funds with varying individual award amounts, duration and renewal; no single collection-wide award.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. Applications open in December and are due in March; the 2026-27 General Application is closed.
apply: Apply through the Cleveland Foundation Scholarships General Application administered by College Now Greater Cleveland.
eligibility: Mostly Northeast Ohio students, including seniors, adults, vocational/professional-development students and some college/graduate applicants. Specific funds set school, county, major, need and GPA rules; some have nationwide or employment-affiliation eligibility. No universal Ohio residence or GPA requirement.
notes: 2026-27 general and corporate/group applications are closed. One application can consider students for multiple funds; criteria differ. Confirm each selected fund’s materials, amount and renewal terms.

name: ScholarshipCONNECT
value: Individual scholarships vary; 2026-27 announcement gives one-time $1,000 awards through $10,000 renewable scholarships. Funds generally cover tuition, fees and books, not room/board; renewal conditions vary.
deadline: Check back December 2026 for 2027-28 applications; exact closing date not published. Typical closing early March; reference letters within one week after application deadline. Prior announcement has inconsistent year wording, so do not use it as a 2027 deadline.
apply: Complete ScholarshipCONNECT general application, then select Opportunities/Ours and submit each eligible award’s added questions or essays. General submission alone does not apply to individual awards. Request required references; track uploads. Acceptance requires student ID, proof of enrollment and donor thank-you.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and current college students in the Greater Dayton region (Montgomery, Miami, Greene, Darke, Preble and northern Warren counties). Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Some funds are merit-only; graduate/professional programs excluded. Trade/career-tech programs included. Renewables receive instructions each March, generally official transcript and year-summary essay due mid-June, with fund-specific college GPA. Foundation’s $3.6 million/1,497 recipient figures are aggregate historical funding.

name: St. Louis Community Foundation scholarships
value: About 80 donor scholarship programs with varying individual amounts, duration and renewal criteria. No single collection-wide award.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund; most listed scholarships are open January to April. Confirm 2027 dates.
apply: My Scholarship Central moved to SurveyMonkey Apply in August 2026. Create a new account even if you previously used the Blackbaud portal; verify a personal email, complete eligibility profile, then complete and submit each matched fund’s tasks. Profile completion alone is not an award application.
eligibility: Students in the St. Louis region and Missouri. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Foundation’s more than $2.5 million to over 700 students is aggregate funding. Most funds open January-April, but dates differ. Older Foundation tips describe Blackbaud and financial-aid documents; follow the new portal’s current fund-specific tasks.

name: CFO scholarships
value: Individual donor scholarships vary. 2026-27 guidance lists $250-$10,000, with many renewable for two-four years; confirm the selected 2027-28 fund’s terms.
deadline: Opens January 1, 2027, for 2027-28; the 2027 deadline is not yet posted. The 2026 deadline was Monday, March 16, 2026.
apply: Create portal account and submit universal application to match eligible funds. Complete and separately submit every matched fund’s supplemental questions. Review scholarship criteria before applying.
eligibility: Central/southern Missouri donor funds serve graduating seniors, current undergraduates, technical-program and some graduate students. Geography, school, field, GPA, need and renewal criteria vary by fund; no common GPA threshold.
notes: About 450 endowments; nearly $1.7 million aggregate for 2026-27, not a student award. Current application page explicitly schedules reopening January 1, 2027.

name: CFNIL scholarship portal
value: More than 125 individual donor scholarships with differing award amounts, duration and renewable conditions; no uniform collection-wide amount.
deadline: Three cycles each year: Fall, November 1 to January 1; Winter (main), December 1 to February 1; Spring, March 1 to April 1. The page does not state the year.
apply: Complete one universal application per cycle in the CFNIL portal (Grant Interface); answers auto-match you to eligible scholarships.
eligibility: High school seniors and older, mainly in Boone, Jo Daviess, McHenry, Ogle, Rock, Stephenson and Winnebago counties (Rockford area), with some funds open USA-wide. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Collection advertises over $500,000 aggregate awards. Recurring fall/winter/spring and rolling cycles differ; awards paid directly to postsecondary school. Some funds have no geographical limit, so Illinois residency is not universal.

name: KZCF scholarships
value: More than 60 individual scholarships/education grants with varying amounts and one-year or multiyear terms. Some can cover approved cost-of-attendance expenses beyond tuition, including housing, transportation, food, insurance and childcare; full attendance coverage is not guaranteed.
deadline: Universal application opens December 1 and closes March 1 annually, with cycle year unstated. Multiyear renewal form sent February and due March 1 annually; emergency funding may be requested year-round.
apply: Complete one universal application in the Kaleidoscope portal to be matched with scholarships.
eligibility: Kalamazoo County residents and high school graduates. Open regardless of citizenship or permanent residence status. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: FAFSA normally required, but Foundation supports applicants unable to file; contact scholarship staff. U.S.-accredited institutions only, no international payments. Multiyear recipients submit annual renewal form and maintain their specific GPA/major criteria. Deferrals require approval; payments directly to institutions.

name: TGKVF scholarships
value: Individual scholarships range $1,000-$12,000, average approximately $3,000. Renewal is fund-specific and competitive; follow-up renewal form required, no automatic continuation.
deadline: 2027-28 application dates not yet posted; the 2026-27 deadline has passed.
apply: Create TGKVF scholarship portal account and follow application/matched-fund instructions. Check personal email for May decisions and acceptance/follow-up forms. Renew eligible award through competitive follow-up form in portal; no IRS tax forms required for application.
eligibility: West Virginia residents statewide, high school seniors and up, attending in-state or out-of-state two-year, four-year, vocational or graduate programs; homeschool students eligible. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Normally one TGKVF award, with Scholars Fund stacking and supplemental Thalheimer Fund exceptions. Payments directly to institution for direct educational expenses; unused funding refunded if withdrawing. Notify Foundation and original institution on transfer; funds reroute after return. More than 115 donor funds; over 500 recipients is aggregate.

name: CFGA scholarships (universal application)
value: Donor awards vary. Published 2026-27 examples include Jim Kennedy up to $40,000 across eight semesters, Nancy Penn Lyons up to $6,000 annually for four years and Pattillo up to $5,500 annually for four years. Confirm 2027-28 amounts and renewal conditions.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. For the 2026-27 cycle, most scholarships opened December 8, 2025 and closed March 2, 2026.
apply: Submit the appropriate portal application and all required attachments/references by its fund deadline. The 2026-27 FAQ requires current FAFSA summary, transcript, fund-specific essays/references and conditional test scores; unofficial transcripts accepted. Renewal invitations are separate, requiring updated academic/enrollment documentation.
eligibility: Each fund sets geography, school, affiliation, GPA, tests and financial-need rules. Many require full-time postsecondary study, but Pattillo allows part-time enrollment while working full time. Mayor’s fund has Atlanta school, residence or qualifying city-employment routes. Employer/college-specific awards have distinct criteria; no universal Georgia-residency requirement.
notes: Published application/FAQ details concern 2026-27. All required references/documents must arrive by closing; missing FAFSA summary is not accepted late under those rules. Awards paid to schools after acceptance; renewable funds require their specific semester/annual follow-up.

name: CFSA scholarships
value: More than 40 donor funds with varying individual amounts, tuition/book/fee coverage, duration and renewal. Each fund sets its own terms.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-2027 scholarship cycle is closed.
apply: Review the official fund list, then use the designated application route: some funds use the Foundation portal, others apply through a school/counselor or institution. Prior FAQ requires FAFSA summary and official/unofficial transcript, with recommendations and test-score information where relevant; all required materials must arrive by deadline.
eligibility: Fund-specific school, county, institution, major, membership, GPA and need criteria. Opportunities include named Alabama schools/communities and institution-restricted awards; there is no common collection-wide GPA or residency criterion.
notes: 2026-27 cycle is closed. Published FAQ describes an older cycle; confirm current attachments when applications reopen. Its essay length is a recommendation, not a universal minimum.

name: Common Scholarship Application
value: 25+ scholarship opportunities through one application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application ran December 1, 2025 to February 3, 2026.
apply: Submit the Community Foundation Tampa Bay Common Scholarship Application on the GrantInterface portal (one application per year during the window).
eligibility: High school seniors, college and technical school students, and people returning to school, primarily from Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco, Hernando and Citrus counties. Individual funds set their own criteria.
notes: Many opportunities serve the five named Florida counties and beyond; individual fund geography and eligibility differ. Foundation also links Apply Tampa Bay for wider matching.

provider: Coastal Community Foundation of South Carolina
name: Coastal Community Foundation scholarships
value: More than 50 donor programs with varying amounts/renewal; current examples include Amanda’s $5,000 per year renewable and Barkley $10,000 per year renewable. Individual renewal conditions and duration differ.
deadline: The application window opens in mid-January and closes in mid-March; exact 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Create an account on the online portal, which matches you to scholarships you qualify for. Submit short-form personal and financial information, a transcript, letters of recommendation and essay answers.
eligibility: Many funds serve Berkeley, Charleston and Dorchester County seniors; some serve other areas or previous recipients, graduate/nontraditional students and nationwide college applicants. Don Rossi example accepts U.S. college juniors/seniors in sports management. School, merit, need and affiliation criteria are fund-specific; South Carolina residency is not universal.
notes: The same portal handles new, renewal, graduate and nontraditional routes. Some named awards require prior participation in a Foundation program. Confirm each fund’s restrictions rather than applying the FAQ’s previous-recipient guidance to every college award.

name: HRCF undergraduate scholarships
value: More than 80 individual undergraduate scholarship funds with differing award amounts. Most are renewable for up to four years with annual form, current transcript, satisfactory standing and fund-specific requirements.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The official page describes a December 1 to March 1 application window with April email notifications.
apply: Submit one portal application and required materials. The 2026-27 checklist includes transcripts, two nonfamily references, personal statement and FAFSA summary/family income documentation; fund-specific exceptions apply, including tax documentation for some vocational programs without federal aid.
eligibility: Most funds serve South Hampton Roads high-school graduates and require financial need/full-time enrollment; some restrict senior status and others have different geographic or educational criteria. Read each selected award’s rules; no universal GPA or residence requirement.
notes: Most awards consider need. Published material checklist explicitly concerns 2026-27; confirm next-cycle financial year and attachments. References should address the applicant for this process, rather than generic recommendation letters.

provider: The Community Foundation of Frederick County
name: CFFC scholarships
value: More than 200 donor scholarships with variable amounts and coverage. General and Trumpower funds support postsecondary study; separate music/athletic opportunities support K-12 activities. Trumpower may provide four total years with continuing eligibility and 2.0 GPA under the 2026 guide.
deadline: General/Trumpower published window March 1-March 31, 2026, not 2027. Music/athletic cycle September 1-September 30, 2026. Trade opening appears as November 1 without year, while 2026 guide lists November 15, 2025-May 1, 2026. Confirm next cycle; no 2027 postsecondary deadline published.
apply: Apply through NextGen using the appropriate program application. A new application is required annually, including renewable awards. 2026 guide requires current transcript with cumulative GPA; need-based consideration requires FAFSA information or qualifying Maryland DREAM Act documentation and need essay. Some music funds require references.
eligibility: General funds primarily serve Frederick County residents; Trumpower serves Carroll County applicants with specified residence/school documentation. Seniors, current undergraduate/graduate/certificate students and nontraditional learners may qualify for full-time or part-time study by fund. Separate music/athletic funds serve K-12 students.
notes: About 60% consider financial need; Maryland DREAM Act route available for qualifying undocumented applicants. School payments and covered costs vary by program. Trumpower residence/school wording differs between current summary and 2026 guide; confirm the applicable route.

name: LCCF scholarship program
value: Individual donor awards vary. The foundation’s current 2027-28 application page says scholarships typically range from $400 to $10,000; some are one-time and others are renewable. Check the selected fund for its amount, duration and eligibility.
deadline: 2027-28 application opens November 2, 2026 and closes February 22, 2027 at 4:00 p.m. No time zone stated. Selected renewable funds receive separate January invitations rather than a new application.
apply: Submit one Scholarship America application for matched funds with current complete transcript. SAT/ACT scores are optional; if supplied and absent from transcript, attach score report. Certain need-based funds require financial/tax documents. Renewal invitees follow separate instructions.
eligibility: Generally Lancaster County school graduates, residents or current undergraduates, with 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale and fund-specific higher requirements. McKonly & Asbury accepts applicants from any U.S. high school/residence who attend specified institutions. Full-time study and major/need restrictions differ by fund.
notes: Foundation publishes the new 2027-28 deadline, while its administrator still displays some 2026-27 fund terms and an older renewal-year label. Selection considers academic record, leadership and need. Recipient receives a college-payable check and delivers it to the institution.

name: CFNJ Scholarships Universal Application
value: More than 135 funds with variable individual awards. Examples include a $5,000 James Moody award offered each year, not a guaranteed annual renewal, and Daniel McKinney up to $20,000 total over four years.
deadline: Open and close dates vary by scholarship; 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Fill out one universal application on the CFNJ GrantInterface portal, then review and apply to the scholarships you may qualify for. Some funds are not on the universal application.
eligibility: Mostly graduating seniors, with some current college/graduate opportunities. Residency, school, major, GPA, need and affiliation vary; Bego example includes New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania residents. No universal New Jersey-residency or GPA requirement.
notes: Over $2 million to 271 scholars is aggregate funding. Renewable recipients must remain full-time at a U.S. institution in good standing. Four-installment awards require transcript, narrative and fall registration by July 15; installments of $5,000+ also require final bill, with August 15 extension. Eight-installment awards require fall materials/bill by August 15 and spring transcript, registration/bill by January 15. Dates recur without cycle year; no reminders sent.

name: RACF Consolidated Scholarship Application
value: 125+ scholarships, including 55+ in the consolidated application. FAQ gives examples from $250 one-time to $40,000 total ($10,000 annually for four years), with fund-specific conditions. Partial educational support, not a guarantee of full cost.
deadline: Consolidated application December 1-February 28 annually, year unstated; portal deadline 11:59 p.m. with no time zone. Individual scholarships have different dates. Required payment documents generally due October 15 of award year unless advance deferral approved.
apply: Complete the consolidated portal application and all matched fund supplements, including required essays, recommendations and unofficial transcript. Upload documents through portal; no paper/email attachments or late extensions. Other funds apply through separate portal, school or community process; some require nomination codes.
eligibility: Mostly Rochester-area residents, with donor-specific school, geographic, major and merit/need criteria. Accredited U.S. colleges, universities and technical/trade schools may qualify. No universal GPA or statewide-residence criterion.
notes: Awards generally paid to school after enrollment and verification. Renewables require satisfactory progress and their specified documents; approved written deferral may allow up to one year. Notify Foundation before transfer, withdrawal or change of use; fund-specific restrictions/refunds apply. Need review permits estimator or family financial information when FAFSA is unavailable.

name: FCCF scholarships
value: More than 150 donor funds with individual amounts and renewal terms varying by fund. A universal application may yield up to four awards, not consideration for only four.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application ran January 8 to April 15, 2026 (extended).
apply: Use Scholarship America online process, with current official transcript, FAFSA summary/SAI and personal statement; references and extra essays depend on fund. The senior checklist limits its recommendation to a named leadership award, while broader checklist describes required references; confirm the selected application’s tasks. Some designated-school awards apply through guidance office.
eligibility: Graduating seniors and current undergraduate/graduate students in accredited degree, vocational, trade or certificate programs. Financial need required. Most have Fairfield County school/residence ties, but named school/institution exceptions accept nonresidents. Seniors generally need 2.7 cumulative GPA; individual and current-college criteria differ. Part-time study may qualify for some funds.
notes: 2025 totals of 445 scholarships/$1.7 million were aggregate, not an individual award. Immigrant/undocumented applicants may contact administrator for application guidance. Required electronic documents must arrive by deadline. Website’s senior and general recommendation checklists differ.

name: GWCF scholarship application
value: More than 140 donor scholarships through one application, with varying individual award amounts and continued eligibility. No uniform collection-wide award.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application opened December 1 and closed February 25, 2026. Decisions are released in early May.
apply: Submit one online application with a transcript, short answer, essay and optional recommendations (required for certain funds); you are matched to funds automatically. FAFSA is not required.
eligibility: Mostly high school seniors from the 60 cities and towns of Worcester County who will enroll full-time in a 2- or 4-year undergraduate program; some funds serve college students, adults or non-residents.
notes: FAFSA not required, but income questions may require tax/benefit information. Recommendations are optional except for named funds. Existing applicants updating an application should edit their account; previous applicants without a current GWCF award are instructed to create a new account when reapplying. Page differs between early-May and mid-June notification guidance.

name: Common Scholarship Application
value: 150+ scholarships; FAQ says individual awards generally $1,000-about $10,000, average $3,000. Nearly 40% renewable for two or four years with fund-specific GPA, criteria and documents; other awards one-year. Covered educational costs differ by fund.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not published. Prior application and all required supplements/references due March 4, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. PST. Award-specific fall/spring verification deadlines assigned in portal; no late materials or year-to-year deferral.
apply: Complete the Common Scholarship Application (short essays; some funds need recommendations or supplements) plus a FAFSA, CA Dream Act Application or Federal Student Aid Estimator result.
eligibility: Seniors, undergraduate/graduate, medical/professional and adult re-entry students at eligible U.S. institutions. Most funds require one full year of San Diego County residency and local parental tax filing, with specified military tax-filing exception. Main guidance lists minimum 2.0 GPA; funds may set higher thresholds. International/undocumented applicants may qualify where fund does not restrict citizenship/status.
notes: Common application automatically matches/submits eligible funds only when all required supplemental questions completed. Financial alternatives include FAFSA, California DREAM Act or Student Aid Estimator. Awards paid to institution after agreement and verification; grades required before each applicable semester. Some require donor thank-you video. Notify Foundation before transfer; no international-institution payments.

name: SRCF scholarships
value: Dozens of donor awards with variable individual amounts; current grid includes $1,000 awards and up to $10,000. Some have multiple payments; duration/renewal conditions depend on selected fund.
deadline: Most scholarships open in December and close in March; 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Create personal-email AcademicWorks account, complete general application, then separately submit matched opportunities. Upload recent transcript including unweighted GPA; references, essay and FAFSA/California DREAM Act report are fund-specific. Need-based applicants unable to file either may submit prior-year complete IRS tax return under current FAQ.
eligibility: Funds serve various Northern California school/county populations and institution/major/demographic groups, including seniors, college, graduate and adult re-entry students. Some graduate/institution awards do not specify county residence. GPA rules differ, including 2.0-4.0+; no common residency/GPA cutoff.
notes: More than $1 million to 400 students is aggregate funding. Financial-aid delays may allow confirmation email/estimated SAI initially, but required final information must be updated. Scholarship claim normally due September 1, year unstated; current page differs between early June and April-May notification guidance.

name: EPIC Scholars Application
value: Over 90 donor scholarship opportunities with differing individual amounts, duration and renewal. Selected renewable funds require annual or semester follow-up; no common collection-wide award.
deadline: 2027 EPIC opening/closing dates not published. Page still carries 2022-23 application dates and 2025 renewal dates; do not treat February 24 as a confirmed next-cycle deadline. Individual funds differ.
apply: Complete EPIC Scholars portal application for matches; separately submit individual scholarships. Upload current official/unofficial transcript with name, school, latest grades and cumulative GPA; named Duncan funds require official transcript. Complete selected fund’s essays/references and all other tasks by deadline.
eligibility: High-school seniors, current college students and returning adults, with fund-specific geography, affiliation, GPA, need and enrollment criteria. Some accept part-time students; no common full-time or Texas-residence rule. Funds generally support eligible U.S. institutions, not international colleges.
notes: Legacy has a separate junior route for Bexar/Webb County students. Foundation stopped administering Whataburger Family Foundation employee fund June 30, 2026; follow the linked new administrator. Renewable funds require their GPA/enrollment and follow-up application; some named funds have probation exceptions. Transfer payments depend on school restrictions and return of original funding.

name: ACF scholarship general application
value: Over 60 donor scholarships with varying individual amounts. Funds cover approved tuition, fees, books, supplies and educational expenses; no single award amount or renewal duration.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 application opened January 15 and closed March 25 at 11:59 p.m. CT.
apply: Complete one general application, submit to receive matches, then finish each matched award’s additional questions. Have current transcripts ready; official preferred. Required references for selected funds use an emailed guided form rather than document upload.
eligibility: Graduating seniors and current college/vocational students, with each donor fund’s geographic, educational and merit/need criteria. Full-time or part-time enrollment may qualify with good standing. No universal GPA or residence cutoff published.
notes: Payment goes directly to accredited school; refunds only for approved reimbursements. Notify Foundation of college/student-ID changes or nonattendance. The posted timeline explicitly concerns 2026, including June 30 acceptance/deferral.

name: WCCF Common Scholarship Application
value: 38 donor scholarships with varying individual amounts, one-year or renewable terms. Fresh Start example up to $5,000 for training/tools/books and related costs; Maltese Cross up to $2,000 annually for five years with 3.0 GPA and at least three credits per semester.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 Common Application opened January 1, 2026 and closed February 15, 2026; the Clough Fellows Scholarship deadline was March 15, 2026.
apply: Create personal portal account, complete common application and its recommended fund tasks, including all required supporting uploads. Some individual/returning-adult funds have separate windows. Interview required for Bill Patterson and certain other funds.
eligibility: Mainly western Colorado graduating seniors, with adult, vocational and active-firefighter funds and some broader Colorado geography. Bill Patterson requires Mesa County Valley District 51 graduation, 3.75 GPA and science/engineering/environment career interest. Fund-specific GPA, school, need and affiliation apply; permanent immigration residency is not universal.
notes: Payments directly to school; FAQ describes splitting awards above $2,000 into two payments and verified-document requirements. Renewables require GPA, other criteria and follow-up documentation; one-year awards differ. Fresh Start supports qualifying vocational training including some for-profit centers. The FAQ still gives a 2023 deadline; use current fund instructions.

name: Innovia scholarships
value: Over 50 scholarships; current individual awards $500-$10,000. Amounts, duration and reapplication differ by fund; some permit annual reapplication with limits. Funds cover tuition, books, fees and school-related expenses for the upcoming academic year.
deadline: Overall 2027-28 application opens December 2, 2026 and closes February 17, 2027. Individual fund descriptions still say December 3-March 4 without updated year; separate external funds have their own windows. Confirm selected fund’s deadline; no time zone stated.
apply: Complete eligibility questionnaire, create MyInnovia account and submit common application/personal statement with current transcripts, required references and financial documentation. Most funds require FAFSA or WASFA; some named funds use separate school/LaunchNW applications.
eligibility: Generally seniors/graduates of the 20-county Eastern Washington/North Idaho service region entering or attending accredited U.S. undergraduate/vocational institutions. Some employer-family funds accept applicants outside the region, and named funds serve other educational stages. Part-time eligibility and GPA/need/affiliation criteria vary. WASFA supports eligible applicants unable to file FAFSA because of immigration status.
notes: Over $500,000 annual funding is aggregate. Institution-payable checks mailed to students; current main guidance says late July. No universal citizenship/permanent-residency rule stated in reviewed current guidance. Reapplication is fund-specific, not automatic renewal; some funds limit years or reduce subsequent awards.

name: CFNLA scholarships
value: Ten named donor scholarships with fund-specific amounts. Community Bank example $1,000 once per winner; unsuccessful applicants may reapply while eligible. Norton explicitly nonrenewable; other individual amounts/duration not stated on collection page.
deadline: 2027 deadlines not yet posted. 2026 deadlines were February 27, 2026 (Thomas E. McElroy, Jr.), March 27, 2026 (most funds) and March 28, 2026 (Community Bank Foundation).
apply: Apply through the CFNLA Scholarship Portal (GrantInterface) with transcripts, ACT scores and essays as each fund requires.
eligibility: Fund-specific school, employer, church, military-dependence, major and academic criteria. Some serve Louisiana seniors; geology fund also supports current undergraduate/graduate students and does not state universal Louisiana residency. Community Bank permits 3.0 high-school GPA OR ACT 20, not both; no collection-wide GPA/test cutoff.
notes: Most funds emphasize achievement; some require need. Hightower uses top 10 students or top 10% of class, rather than only top 10%. Haley is a separate route for prior Hightower recipients. Community Bank requires eligible school acceptance before payment.

name: CFGB scholarship process
value: Individual awards approximately $1,000-$6,000 for approved academic-year educational expenses. No summer funding; renewability/duration are not specified on the reviewed collection pages.
deadline: Application process currently closed; 2027 dates not published. FAQ lists May 1 for college choice/financial information, while the older initiatives page also gives May 15 for financial information. Confirm next cycle’s document deadline.
apply: When process opens, submit required financial-aid report, all college award letters and grades online. Official transcript not required; high-school report card should show at least two marking periods, college applicants current grade report. If financial package is pending, obtain estimated school amounts and confirm deadline.
eligibility: Permanent mailing address in one of the eight Western New York counties: Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie, Genesee, Niagara, Orleans or Wyoming. At least 2.0 GPA and acceptance at an accredited nonprofit U.S. school for full-time undergraduate study. Limited graduate funds in specified fields have separate rules.
notes: About $3 million to nearly 3,000 students in 2025 is aggregate. Awards primarily need-based, with strong preference for Pell-eligible applicants attending school in the region; some weigh achievement/service. Changing schools after award cancels scholarship under the posted FAQ. Permanent local address can qualify when studying elsewhere.
